title: Profiling of mouse macrophage lipidome using direct infusion shotgun mass spectrometry
protocol: Set up a clean workbench with an isoflurane chamber, dissection tray, and two beakers containing water and 70% ethanol.
Clean all the tools with 70% ethanol (EtOH).
Place a 50 mL centrifuge tube on a rack and fill it with 30 mL of ice-cold PBS for bone collection.
Sacrifice mice in an isoflurane chamber with a 5% concentration for about 5 minutes.
Assess the death of the animal by checking for lack of heartbeat and pedal reflex (firm toe pinch).
Spray the deceased animal with 70% ethanol and place it in the dissection tray.
Secure limbs to the tray with 25G x 5/8 inch needles.
Remove the skin, fur, and muscle from the legs first.
Isolate the femur and tibia using tweezers and scissors.
Grasp the bone with tweezers and cut away excess tissue around the ends of the bone.
Cut down each leg along the separated skin with the foot still attached to the leg.
Remove the foot and place the leg in a PBS-filled centrifuge tube.
Fill a 10 mL syringe with 10 mL of ice-cold PBS and attach a 26G x 5/8 inch needle for each leg.
Place the legs on a sterile 10 cm tissue culture dish.
Cut the distal end of the tibia to flush the marrow.
Place the isolated femur and tibia on a separate 10 cm tissue culture dish.
Place a 40 μM cell strainer on a 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Pierce bone at the ends with syringe and flush bone with PBS into the cell strainer until it becomes translucent white, using between 3 – 5 mL of PBS per bone.
Rinse the cell strainer with 5 mL of ice-cold PBS for maximum recovery.
Spin down the bone marrow at 365 × g for 7 min at room temperature and aspirate off the PBS.
Resuspend the bone marrow in 3 mL of RBC lysis buffer and place at room temperature for 3 minutes.
Neutralize the RBC lysis buffer by adding 7 mL of ice-cold PBS.
Spin down the bone marrow at 365 × g for 5 min at room temperature.
Aspirate off the PBS and resuspend the bone marrow in 20 mL of BMDM medium for cell counting.
Determine the number of live macrophages using a hematocytometer or an automated cell counter, with trypan blue staining or AO and PI dyes for assessment.
Seed 16 – 20 million monocyte precursors per 15 cm tissue culture-treated culture dishes for differentiation by day 6 of differentiation to prevent overgrowth.
Add 25 mL of macrophage media per dish.
On day 4 of macrophage differentiation, change the medium by aspirating 20 mL of spent macrophage media and replacing it with 20 mL of fresh macrophage media.
On day 6, remove 23 mL of macrophage media and replenish it with 15 mL of fresh media.
Tilt the plate on an angle without spilling the medium.
Gently scrape the tissue culture plate with cell lifters.
Transfer the macrophages into a 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Pipette the cell suspension to ensure cell dissociation.
Determine the number of live macrophages using a hematocytometer or automated cell counter.
Pipette 9 × 10^5 BMDMs into each well of a 6-well plate.
Top up the media to a total of 2 mL per well.
Disperse the cells equally by gently rocking the plate back and forth.
Place the plates on a flat surface in a 5% CO2 incubator at 37°C.
Warm up the BMDM experimental media 15 minutes prior to macrophage treatment.
Label 50 mL centrifuge tubes.
Pipette 20 mL of macrophage experimental media into each tube.
Add stimuli or vehicle controls into the labeled tubes.
Vortex the tubes to ensure proper mixing.
Aspirate the media from the wells.
Use a P1000 micropipette to transfer 2 mL of experimental media containing the appropriate stimulus to each well.
Gently rock the plate to ensure proper mixing.
Place the plates on a flat surface in a 5% CO2 incubator at 37°C.
Visually inspect each well under the microscope prior to live cell staining for cell counts.
Stain each well with 1.25 mM Calcein-AM dissolved in DMEM to a final concentration of 1.45 μM.
Image the plates on a Molecular Devices ImageXpress XL instrument using a 10× objective (Nikon Plan Fluor, 0.3 NA).
Capture 20 high magnification fluorescence images for each well section covering 24% of total well surface area.
Assess total live cell number with MetaXpress Software with Powercore using the Multi-wavelength cell scoring module.
Pre-chill all glass tubes, PBS, and collection tube rack before sample collection.
Collect samples directly into Kimble tubes or glass tubes and store accordingly.
Combine two wells of cells as a single replicate for analysis.
Remove culturing media from each well after staining.
Add 1 mL of ice-cold PBS to each well.
Scrape the cells with cell lifters and transfer them into glass tubes or 10 mL Kimble tubes.
Spin collected samples at 365 × g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Aspirate the media without performing additional washes using PBS.
Conduct scraping and collecting of cells on ice.
Snap freeze the tubes containing aspirated PBS for -80°C storage (up to 6 months) or proceed directly to lipid extraction.
Use glassware throughout the entire lipid extraction process to minimize PEG and fatty acids contamination.
Warm frozen cell pellet for 30 min to ambient temperature by placing them on a clean bench top.
Add 0.9 mL of water to the sample in each Kimble tube.
Add 2 mL of methanol to the sample in each Kimble tube.
Add 0.9 mL of dichloromethane to the sample in each Kimble tube.
Add 0.1 mL of the Lipidyzer Internal Standard Mixture to the extracts.
Invert the 10 mL Kimble tubes 4 to 8 times.
Set the extracts on the benchtop at room temperature for 30 min.
Add 1 mL of water and 0.9 mL of dichloromethane to the extracts.
Invert the extracts 4 to 8 times.
Centrifuge the extracts at 1,200 × g for 10 min at room temperature.
Transfer the bottom organic layer using a glass Pasteur pipette to a new 10 mL Kimble tube.
Take the lower phase with as little upper phase and interface material as possible.
Add another 1.8 mL of dichloromethane to the original extract Kimble tubes.
Invert the original extracts 4 to 8 times.
Centrifuge the inverted extracts at 1,200 × g for 10 min at room temperature.
Take the bottom layers and add them to previous aliquots in step 35.
Cap Kimble tubes containing organic bottom layers and gently vortex for 3 to 5 seconds.
Dry combined bottom layers using an EZ-2 Elite evaporator under low boiling point conditions with heat off, at room temperature, and fixed speed.
Alternatively, dry samples using a nitrogen evaporator.
Briefly vortex the dried samples in Kimble tubes.
Gently pipette the mixture up and down using a glass Pasteur pipette to wash off any stuck material onto the tube walls.
Transfer samples to 1 mL Robovials with 100 μL fixed glass insert using glass Pasteur pipettes.
Centrifuge the Robovials in 931 × g for 10 min at 10°C.
Load Robovials into autosampler for Lipidyzer mass spectrometry analysis.
